frequency_question: How often does an active macroprudential regime transition a dormant capital buffer to an active positive setting within a defined multi-month policy window?
membership_rule: Members are established post-2016 financial regulatory jurisdictions with operational countercyclical capital buffer frameworks; non-members are developing economies or jurisdictions without independent macroprudential frameworks.

cases.name: Bank of England CCyB hike to 1%
Bank of England CCyB reimplementation to 2%
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation cycle
Bank of England CCyB restoration to 2%

provenance_note: 7 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.4x)
coverage_note: 7 named major cases; estimated roughly 10 total across advanced G10 economies utilizing active CCyB frameworks.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market jurisdictions with non-comparable banking sector structures.
skeleton: 7 major economy activation/increase events identified across 4 core jurisdictions with active frameworks over a 10-year observation window, averaging approximately 0.7 structured tightening events per year globally per major peer central bank when credit-to-GDP gaps or systemic risk warnings flash.
multiplier: 7 historical documented activation instances divided by total monitored systemic risk evaluation windows where precursors were visible.
validity_reason: Macroprudential frameworks and Basel III institutional norms remain stable over multi-year horizons, updating only with major regulatory overhauls.
